q.description: Parameter defines the keyword to search ads for, like a keyword search in the Ad Library (e.g., `coffee` or `running shoes`). It returns the ads that match the keyword, whatever their advertiser: to get the ads of an advertiser, use page_id. Either q or page_id should be set. They can also be used together to get the advertiser's ads that match the keyword.

page_id.description: Parameter defines the Facebook page ID of the advertiser whose ads you want to get (e.g., `15087023444` for Nike). Page IDs are available in `page_id` of the ads in the results. Either q or page_id should be set. They can also be used together to get the advertiser's ads that match the keyword.

country.description: Parameter defines the country where the ads were shown. It's a two-letter country code (e.g., `US` for the United States, or `DE` for Germany), or `ALL` (default) for all countries. Head to the Meta Ad Library countries page for a full list of supported countries.

search_type.description: Parameter defines the type of keyword search. It can be set to `keyword_unordered` (default) to search for the words of the query in any order, or `keyword_exact_phrase` to search for the query as an exact phrase.

ad_type.description: Parameter defines the category of the ads. It defaults to `all`. Available options: `all` - All ads `political_and_issue_ads` - Issues, elections or politics `housing_ads` - Housing `employment_ads` - Employment `financial_products_and_services_ads` - Financial products and services The Ad Library doesn't offer `political_and_issue_ads` in the countries of the European Union, where it returns no ads. Their ads about social issues, elections or politics are in the results of `all`.

active_status.description: Parameter defines whether the ads are still running. It defaults to `active`. Available options: `active` - Active ads `inactive` - Inactive ads `all` - Active and inactive ads

media_type.description: Parameter defines the type of media of the ads. It defaults to `all`. Available options: `all` - All media types `image` - Images `meme` - Memes `image_and_meme` - Images and memes `video` - Videos `none` - No image or video

publisher_platforms.description: Parameter defines the platforms the ads were shown on. It's a comma-separated list of platforms (e.g., `facebook,instagram`). It defaults to all platforms. Available options: `facebook` - Facebook `instagram` - Instagram `audience_network` - Audience Network `messenger` - Messenger `whatsapp` - WhatsApp `threads` - Threads

content_languages.description: Parameter defines the languages of the ads. It's a comma-separated list of two-letter language codes (e.g., `en` for English, or `en,es` for English and Spanish). It defaults to all languages.

start_date.description: Parameter defines the start of the date range of the ads, in the `YYYY-MM-DD` format (e.g., `2026-01-01`). Like the Ad Library's impressions by date filter, it returns the ads shown during the date range, whenever they started running. It can't be in the future.

end_date.description: Parameter defines the last day of the date range of the ads, in the `YYYY-MM-DD` format (e.g., `2026-03-31`).

sort_by.description: Parameter defines the sorting of the results. It defaults to `impressions_high_to_low`, like the Ad Library. Available options: `most_recent` - Most recent `impressions_high_to_low` - Impressions: high to low `impressions_low_to_high` - Impressions: low to high The Ad Library only offers `impressions_low_to_high` for ads about social issues, elections or politics, the only ads it shows the impressions of.

next_page_token.description: Parameter defines the next page token. It is used for retrieving the next page results. Each page has up to 30 results, like the Ad Library. The next page token can be found in the SerpApi JSON response: `serpapi_pagination -> next_page_token`

engine.description: Set parameter to `meta_ad_library` to use the Meta Ad Library API engine.

no_cache.description: Parameter will force SerpApi to fetch the Meta Ad Library results even if a cached version is already present. A cache is served only if the query and all parameters are exactly the same. Cache expires after 1h. Cached searches are free, and are not counted towards your searches per month. It can be set to `false` (default) to allow results from the cache, or `true` to disallow results from the cache. no_cache and async parameters should not be used together.

async.description: Parameter defines the way you want to submit your search to SerpApi. It can be set to `false` (default) to open an HTTP connection and keep it open until you got your search results, or `true` to just submit your search to SerpApi and retrieve them later. In this case, you'll need to use our Searches Archive API to retrieve your results. async and no_cache parameters should not be used together. async should not be used on accounts with Ludicrous Speed enabled.

zero_trace.description: Enterprise only. Parameter enables ZeroTrace mode. It can be set to `false` (default) or `true`. Enable this mode to skip storing search parameters, search files, and search metadata on our servers. This may make debugging more difficult.

api_key.description: Parameter defines the SerpApi private key to use.

output.description: Parameter defines the format of the result. It can be set to `json` (default) to get a structured JSON of the results, `html` to get the raw HTML retrieved, or `md` to get a Markdown-formatted version optimized for LLMs and AI agents.

json_restrictor.description: Parameter defines the fields you want to include in the output, reducing payload size for faster response. See the JSON Restrictor documentation for more details.
